output.sql:
WITH units AS (
  SELECT p.product_id, p.sku, p.product_name, SUM(ol.quantity) AS units_sold
  FROM marts.fct_order_lines ol
  JOIN marts.fct_orders o ON o.order_id = ol.order_id
  JOIN marts.dim_products p ON p.product_id = ol.product_id
  WHERE o.status = 'completed'
    AND o.order_date >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.order_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY p.product_id, p.sku, p.product_name
), ranked AS (
  SELECT product_id, sku, product_name, units_sold,
         RANK() OVER (ORDER BY units_sold DESC) AS rnk
  FROM units
)
SELECT product_id, sku, product_name, units_sold
FROM ranked
WHERE rnk = 1;
output.explanation:
This query finds the product with the most units sold in completed orders placed in 2025. It adds up the quantity on each order line, keeping only orders with status = 'completed' and an order date in calendar year 2025, and groups the totals by product. If two or more products tie for first place, it returns all of them.

I assumed the status value is spelled 'completed' in lowercase; if the data uses a different spelling, the filter needs to change. I filtered on order status rather than the is_revenue flag because you asked about completed orders specifically.
